messages:
alex: quick follow-up to the provenance handshake RFC — I pushed a pared-down proposal that avoids shipping full envelopes on every event. TL;DR: store a tiny pointer + checksum, materialize full provenance only for audits/backfills.
maria: link? want the diff.
alex: https://docs.internal/rfc/provenance-slimdown — main change is `token_provenance_ref` instead of full `provenance_body`. tiny JSON example: { \"ref\": \"p-<fingerprint>\", \"crc\": \"abc123\" }
raj: tradeoffs: if ingest stores only a ref, how do we guarantee availability later? GC/replication risks.
taylor: and correctness windows — if the ref points to data that was compacted we could fail audits.
alex: proposal adds a low-retention hot-store (7d) for fast fetches + a cold-store archive for long-term. the ref includes an \"era\" tag so we can route fetches.
maria: any numbers on how often audits request the full body? don't want fetch-heavy query-time patterns.
raj: rough historical numbers: ~0.5% of billing events ever trigger a forensic fetch. most audits are aggregate-only.
taylor: 0.5% is ok, but tenant disputes can spike. need an SLO for fetch latency and clear fallback behavior.
alex: fetch path idea: try hot-store first (fast). if miss, return 202 and kick background rehydrate from cold-store, notify ops.
sre-bot: [sim] 99th fetch latency to hot-store = 120ms, cold-store cold-start = 6s.
raj: 6s is acceptable for human audits, not for automated reconciles that expect sub-second. for reconcile jobs we should auto-fallback to a compatible cached snapshot.
maria: provenance may include redacted content. refs must preserve redaction guarantees and be KMS-protected.
alex: agreed — refs point to encrypted, redaction-aware payloads; decrypt keys gated by KMS roles. add a metadata field `redaction_level` on the ref.
taylor: what about ledger semantics and GC? we must not break append-only proofs.
raj: keep small verification artifacts (fingerprint + merkle-root) with each billing event. full bodies GC'd after TTL but proofs remain to verify historical accounting.
alex: ingest event sketch: `{"event_id":"e..","tenant_id":"t..","usage_tokens":123,"provenance_ref":{"ref":"p-<fp>","crc":"abc123","era":"hot","redaction_level":"partial"},"proof_root":"r.."}`
maria: backward compatibility — downstream connectors expect full envelope sometimes. migration path?
alex: v1 adapter will emit both `provenance_ref` and `provenance_body` during a transition window. per-connector feature flag to flip.
taylor: rollout ops: pre-warm hot-store for high-SLA tenants before flipping to avoid noisy fallbacks.
raj: add a synthetic load test that simulates 1000-tenant audit day to catch scale issues.
sre-bot: scheduled job created: `prov-sim-load-1000` starting 1705060000.
deploy-bot: RFC published to docs.internal and flagged for product review.
maria: metrics to monitor: `provenance.fetch.rate`, `provenance.miss.rate`, `audit.retry.count`, `prov.fetch.latency_p95`.
alex: experiment plan: 5% tenants for 2 weeks, monitor metrics and incidents. expand if fetch miss <1% and no missing-provenance incidents.
taylor: update billing SLA doc to note possible 202 for deep-audit payloads and expected rehydrate times. ops must be clear to customers.
alex: will draft rollout playbook, migration checklist, and the billing note. thanks all :thumbsup:
